nodes.label: Fire Nation Goose Voting Carousel
nodes.description: Screenshot of the GooseOS goose art voting carousel shown inside a Win95-style window titled 'belles-lettres.exe'. Displays three horizontally arranged photos of geese/birds interacting with people in outdoor settings. The name 'fire-nation' derives from the visible caption text 'everything changed when the fire nation attacked', a pop-culture reference (Avatar: The Last Airbender meme) used as humorous alt-text or caption for the goose imagery. The UI features left/right chevron navigation arrows for cycling through goose art submissions, and two small icon buttons below (likely upvote/flag controls). The window uses classic Windows 95 chrome: gray title bar, minimize/maximize/close buttons in the top-right corner. The desktop background is flat gray and the taskbar at the bottom shows a '/start' button, consistent with the Win95 aesthetic of GooseOS.
ui_components: Horizontal image carousel with 3 visible goose art photos
Two small icon/vote buttons (star and flag icons)
Win95 title bar with minimize/maximize/close controls
nodes.color_scheme: Windows 95 system gray (#c0c0c0) with standard title bar blue-gray, white window content area, black text, and natural-color photographs in the carousel
visible_text: everything changed when the fire nation attacked
nodes.feature_shown: Goose art voting carousel — the voting/gallery page of GooseOS where users browse and vote on uploaded goose artwork
design_decisions: Win95 window metaphor applied to a modern web app for retro aesthetic
Horizontal carousel layout for goose art browsing
Humorous meme caption ('everything changed when the fire nation attacked') as content/alt-text for goose images
Minimal vote controls (icon buttons) beneath the carousel
Consistent gray desktop with taskbar to reinforce desktop OS illusion

nodes.label: belles-lettres.exe Win95 Window
nodes.description: The Win95-style application window containing the goose voting carousel. Titled 'belles-lettres.exe', referencing fine arts/literature in a tongue-in-cheek naming convention for a goose art gallery. Has standard Win95 window chrome: title bar, minimize/maximize/close buttons.

nodes.label: Goose Art Voting Carousel Component
nodes.description: The core UI component visible in this screenshot: a horizontally scrollable carousel displaying three goose art photos side by side, with left/right chevron navigation arrows and vote controls below. Implemented in legacy frontend using js/vote/carousel.js (D3.js or jQuery based).

nodes.label: Fire Nation Caption Meme Text
nodes.description: Visible caption text reading 'everything changed when the fire nation attacked' — a well-known internet meme referencing Avatar: The Last Airbender, applied humorously to describe goose aggression imagery in the carousel. This text names the screenshot file 'fire-nation.png'.

nodes.label: Win95 Desktop Taskbar with /start Button
nodes.description: Bottom taskbar element of the GooseOS desktop showing a '/start' button, consistent with the Windows 95 desktop metaphor applied throughout GooseOS. Uses command-style naming (/start) blending Win95 aesthetics with CLI/terminal aesthetics.
